newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - Aegon lifts Q1 profit 24 pct, ups forecast.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Aegon lifts Q1 profit 24 pct, ups forecast.

text.p: Dutch insurer Aegon NV announced a 24 percent increase in first quarter profits to 403.4 million guilders ($211.9 million) on Thursday.

Aegon also said it expected 1997 full-year net profits and earnings per share (EPS), excluding acquisitions, to be 15 percent higher than in 1996, a bigger increase than it had forecast in March when it saw EPS rising 10-12 percent.
The improved outlook and the result, which was at the upper end of forecasts, prompted analysts to upgrade their expectations of full year profit.
"The increase in net income is particularly firm as a result of the continued trend of buoyant stock markets and a further strengthening of Aegon's main currencies," Aegon said.
After some initial gyrations after the result, the company's shares ended at 143.70 guilders, up 2.10 despite the Dutch share market closing slightly weaker.
The company said autonomous profit growth in the first three months of 1997, excluding acquisitions, start-ups, divestments and exchange rate differences, was 18 percent.
Aegon said said it had decided to "raise the bar" by upgrading profit forecasts for the full year of 1997.

"Barring unforeseen circumstances...and not taking into account the impact of the acquisition of Providian, we expect an increase in 1997 net profit and earnings per share in guilders of some 15 percent," Aegon said.
Aegon earned a net profit of 1.57 billion guilders in 1996, or 5.93 guilders per share.
Aegon said that, on top of that, its planned acquisition of the insurance activities of U.S. group Providian Corporation would have a positive impact on earnings per share.
It expects to finalise the $3.5 billion deal by June or July.
It is the largest U.S. acquisition by a Dutch company and the biggest acquisition in the U.S. life insurance industry.

Aegon said pre-tax profits from life insurance, clearly the largest of its businesses, grew 26 percent in the first quarter, with accident and health results increasing 31 percent, general insurance by 35 percent and banking by 23 percent.
In the Netherlands, its largest market, pre-tax results jumped 29 percent, with life earnings growing especially due to better interest rate results and increased share values.
Results from the Americas division rose 19 percent in guilder terms on a steady performance from all core activities.
Analysts were positive about the result, which was at the upper end of forecasts ranging between 363.5 million and 405 million guilders.
"It's much better than had been expected. It was better across the board," said Andreas de Groot of MeesPierson.
He said the company's forecast of 15 percent growth in profits from 1996 to 1997 was conservative.
IRIS analyst Bart van der Feen was particularly impressed with premium growth.
"I am increasing my EPS estimates for the full year to 7.20 guilders from 7.00 guilders, including Providian," he added. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
